name: שַׁמָּה
gloss: desolation, astonishment; or a short form of Shimeah
summary: Borne by a son of Reuel son of Esau, a chief of Edom (Gen 36:13, 17; 1Ch 1:37); by Jesse's third son, David's brother, passed over when Samuel came to anoint (1Sa 16:9; 17:13), who is also called שִׁמְעָה and שִׁמְעָא (2Sa 13:3; 1Ch 2:13); by Shammah son of Agee, one of David's three mighty men, who stood in the field of lentils when the people fled and struck the Philistines (2Sa 23:11–12, spelled שַׁמָּא); by Shammah the Harodite (2Sa 23:25), Shammoth (שַׁמּוֹת) in 1Ch 11:27; by Shammah the Hararite, father of Jonathan (2Sa 23:33); and, as שַׁמָּא, by a man of Asher (1Ch 7:37). The name is the noun שַׁמָּה “desolation, astonishment” as it stands; but scripture does not explain it, and for David's brother the same man is named from שׁמע, so it may be a short form of that name.

evidence.note: “Nahath and Zerah, שַׁמָּה and Mizzah”, sons of Reuel.
“Then Jesse made שַׁמָּה pass by, and he said, Neither has Yahweh chosen this one.”
“Jonadab son of שִׁמְעָה, David's brother”: the same brother under a שׁמע form.
“Abinadab the second, and שִׁמְעָא the third.”
“After him was שַׁמָּא son of Agee the Hararite … he stood in the midst of the plot and defended it, and struck the Philistines, and Yahweh worked a great salvation.”
“שַׁמּוֹת the Harorite”, the same man in the Chronicler's list.
The common noun: “horror (שַׁמָּה) has seized me”.
The common noun: “this whole land will become a ruin and a desolation (לְשַׁמָּה)”.

note: Takes v.ea.ag (שַׁמָּה, 14 tokens, of which Jer 5:30; 8:21; 51:37; Ezk 23:33; Isa 24:12; Psa 46:9 are the common noun by spelling) and v.ea.ae (שַׁמָּא, 2Sa 23:11; 1Ch 7:37). TIPNR files David's brother as Shimeah@1Sa.16.9 with Shammah as one of his forms. 1Ch 11:27 שַׁמּוֹת is tagged through Shammah@2Sa.23.25 (TIPNR's form Shammoth). Shamhuth (שַׁמְהוּת, 1Ch 27:8), likely the same Harorite, is a different spelling and not included. Shammai (שַׁמַּי) is not given an entry: see the shamem note. Whether the name means “desolation” at all, or is a hypocoristic of a שׁמע name (as David's brother's other names suggest), is open.
